name: Boxed-radio intent picker (RadioGroup, no dot)
description: A cardless single-select where each option is a full-width bordered box (not a dot+label) wraps Radix RadioGroupPrimitive.Root/.Item directly rather than the dot-style Radio primitive — Radix still owns roving focus/arrow-keys/role=radiogroup, we style the Item as border-2 border-border-strong box with data-[state=checked]:border-primary. Keep it controlled with value={state} ('' = none) NOT value={x||undefined}, else React warns uncontrolled->controlled on first select. cn() silently deleted every design-system font-size token. tailwind-merge only knows Tailwind's STOCK font sizes (text-sm, text-base, ...) and classifies every other text-* as a text COLOUR. Resonance's whole type scale is custom (--text-heading-md, --text-body-lg, ...), so cn("text-heading-md font-medium", "text-muted") resolved to "font-medium text-muted" — the 22px heading rendered at the inherited size — and in the reverse order cn("bg-primary text-on-primary", "text-body-lg") dropped the COLOUR, turning the brand Follow button's white label into #2b2b2b on #6034ff. Latent since the scale was added; it also hit the existing onboarding composites (weave-interview-rail Message, profile-draft-panels). Invisible to typecheck, lint and RTL — only measuring getComputedStyle on a real render exposed it.
resolution: Register the scale with extendTailwindMerge in packages/ui/src/lib/cn.ts: extend.classGroups['font-size'] = [{ text: FONT_SIZES }] listing every --text-* suffix. Locked by src/lib/cn.test.ts (both orders, plus stock conflicts still resolving). RULE: adding a --text-* token to theme.css means editing FONT_SIZES in cn.ts in the same change — noted in packages/ui/CLAUDE.md.

name: Offline pixel verification for @resonance/ui when no app route exists yet
description: ADR-0019 wants design.png vs app.png, but a ui-package crewmate often builds components BEFORE the route that hosts them (here: /discover is step 5, the pixel-diff is step 6). Building blind is how drift ships. Working substitute that needs no dev server and no Figma calls: (1) a throwaway vitest spec in packages/ui renders the real components with renderToStaticMarkup; (2) compile the REAL token CSS with tailwindcss's compile() API — feed it src/styles/theme.css with the @source directives stripped, resolve @import via a loadStylesheet that require.resolve's tailwindcss/index.css, and pass the class names scraped out of the rendered markup as the candidate list; (3) write one self-contained HTML file; (4) screenshot and, crucially, MEASURE it with @playwright/test from apps/web — page.evaluate getBoundingClientRect + getComputedStyle on each element and compare the numbers to the frame spec in design/manifest. Delete the spec afterwards so it never runs in CI. The measurement is the part that pays: eyeballing the screenshot looked correct while fonts were 14px instead of 22px and the Follow label was dark on brand. Do not use the Playwright MCP for this — its Chromium channel is unresolved in this repo; drive @playwright/test directly from apps/web, which has it installed.

content: Tailwind v4 generates spacing utilities from --spacing by calc, so off-scale DESIGN values are still token-derived, not arbitrary: the Figma tab's 17px gap is gap-4.25 (4.25 x 4px), verified by compiling it. Reach for a fractional scale step before an arbitrary [17px] bracket — packages/ui has zero arbitrary-px classes and should stay that way. Reserve a new theme token for values with a semantic ROLE (e.g. --color-image-placeholder #d9d9d9, the ProfileImg plate, which is genuinely off the neutral ramp), not for one-off spacing.

name: Discovery result chrome: controlled composites over the core discovery contract
description: packages/ui/src/components/{search-bar,result-tabs,creator-result-row,creator-result-list,discovery-empty-states}.tsx — the /discover chrome (Figma 1443:78153). Same idiom as WeaveInterviewRail/ProfileDraftPanels: props down, callbacks up, bound to @resonance/core types (CreatorResult, ResultKind, FollowState) rather than parallel shapes. Three decisions worth reusing. (1) PRESENTATION ORDER LIVES IN UI: core's RESULT_KINDS declaration order is not the tab order, so ResultTabs exports its own RESULT_TAB_ORDER — core says so explicitly. (2) THE THIRD FOLLOW STATE IS NOT A BOOLEAN: 'unknown' (signed out) renders the default Follow affordance but OMITS aria-pressed instead of setting it false, because 'not followed' and 'we cannot know' are different claims; the parent turns the click into a sign-in prompt. (3) TWO EMPTY STATES, ONE FILE: a dataless tab (ComingSoonState — badge + bordered muted panel) and a zero-result search (NoResultsState — plain centred prose, role=status) are separate components colocated so the must-stay-distinct invariant is readable in one place, with an RTL test asserting distinctness on five axes. Also note the DOM-attribute trap: naming a list prop 'results' collides with React's deprecated numeric HTMLAttributes.results and needs an Omit.

name: ADR-0019 parity by measurement: DOM geometry + byte samples + band diffs, not eyeballing
description: A /discover parity pass that holds up. Three complementary instruments, none sufficient alone: (1) LIVE DOM — a Playwright script reading getBoundingClientRect() + getComputedStyle() per element gives exact CSS geometry, computed colours (rgb(96,52,255) = #6034ff), font shorthand and radii to compare against design.md's frame numbers; it caught that the content column, search bar, tab bar, tab rule, row pitch, avatar slot and button all match EXACTLY. (2) PIXEL BYTES — sharp resolved from node_modules/.pnpm (it is not a declared dep anywhere) extracting 1x1 regions, plus a colour histogram over a band when a point sample lands on the wrong feature; that is what proved the Follow fill is #6034ff in BOTH images and that the page background differs by exactly 13/channel (#ffffff vs #f2f2f2). (3) BAND DIFFS — downscale app.png 3024->1512, then diff design x=527 against app x=514 to APPLY the ratified 13px offset: the tab underline row comes out 0.00%% different, and the search-bar band drops 3.60%% -> 2.07%%, which turns the ratified delta into a measurement instead of an assertion. Choose the tolerance deliberately: >12 is dominated by the flat 13/channel background delta, >20 isolates structure. Also: reuse the frame's own sample query ('Tinctures') so the captured SearchBar carries the designed text, and seed representative rows for the capture then delete them.

Figma reports a chip as '12px padding, 2px stroke, 18px line height, 42px tall' — but building that literally in CSS renders 46px. Figma draws strokes INSIDE the padding box; CSS borders add outside it. The same bug hit the chip panel (24px padding + 1px border rendered 192px instead of the drawn 190px). It is invisible by eye: the first TopicPicker capture looked correct while every chip was 4px too tall and the whole column was 2px off-centre.
resolution: Subtract the border width from the padding: p-2.5 (10px) + border-2 gives the drawn 42px chip; p-5.75 (23px) + border gives the drawn 190px panel. Both are real Tailwind v4 spacing utilities (calc from --spacing), not arbitrary bracket values. After the correction the panel, all three chip rows and the button land at the frame's EXACT y offsets. Only measurement catches this — getBoundingClientRect per element against the frame numbers, never eyeballing the screenshot.

name: Chip multi-select: shared cva + native checkboxes, not a forked chip
description: TopicPicker (Figma 1554:79520) needed a selectable chip when packages/ui already shipped a read-only Tag. Rather than fork, tag.tsx now exports a tagVariants cva whose three states map 1:1 onto the Figma Tags component set 1409:46348 (outline=Added, selectable=Selectable, selected=Selectable/Selected), and Tag consumes it. tagVariants is exported SEPARATELY from the Tag element because the chip's look and the chip's semantics have different owners: a read-only chip is a span role=listitem, a chip that toggles a choice must be a form control. Forcing both through Tag means lying about the role or shipping a second chip that drifts. Same split buttonVariants already sets. The picker composes tagVariants onto a <label> wrapping a visually-hidden native <input type=checkbox>, inside a <fieldset aria-labelledby> pointed at the h1. Radix has no checkbox-group and ToggleGroup is not installed; native checkboxes need zero hand-rolled ARIA (Space toggles, each chip tabbable, 'Wellness, checkbox, checked') AND submit through a plain form POST when several share one name — which is exactly what the Server Action consuming them wants. Chose every-chip-tabbable over roving tabindex deliberately.

The offline pixel-verification harness (mx-7f1e52) rendered the Resonance mark BLACK instead of its spectrum gradient. Not a component bug: ResonanceMark's SVG gradient stops reference var(--color-brand-cyan) etc., and compiler.build(candidates) only emits the @theme variables that a MATCHED UTILITY references. No utility used the brand namespace, so Tailwind tree-shook it and every var() resolved to nothing. Any token referenced only from inline SVG/style attributes — never through a class — vanishes the same way, and the harness silently renders a wrong image you then diff against the design.
resolution: Append synthetic candidates for the var()-only tokens to the scraped class list (text-brand-cyan, text-brand-indigo, …) so Tailwind keeps the namespace. Also worth pinning: capture at deviceScaleFactor 1 into the design frame's own box (1512x982) so design.png and app.png are the same size and diff with NO rescaling — the previous pass captured at 3024 and had to downscale before every band diff.
